title: The Street Philosophy of Garry Winogrand

description.main: Geoff Dyer writes on one hundred Winogrand photographs from the Center for Creative Photography archive, including eighteen unpublished color images.
description.extended:
Geoff Dyer's book of one hundred Winogrand photographs, each paired with a short essay of his own, treats a major street photographer as a subject for a writer's close looking.

The selection comes from the Winogrand archive at the Center for Creative Photography and includes eighteen color photographs not published before. It is modeled on John Szarkowski's book on Atget. The sequence follows the chronology and geography of Winogrand's life and covers most of his themes, and Dyer's responses to the pictures are unorthodox and often funny.

Winogrand (1928-1984) ranks with Diane Arbus and Lee Friedlander among the most important photographers of the 1960s and 1970s. Dyer, an award-winning writer, has admired his work for years, and he offers the book as an education in seeing.
